legend: Flow cytometry of T-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma at diagnosis. Leukaemic blasts (red) show an immature T-lineage immunophenotype with expression of cCD3, dim to absent sCD3, and variable CD34. Compared with normal mature T cells (green and magenta), the leukaemia shows abnormal expression of increased CD7, decreased CD5, decreased CD45, and variable CD4 and CD8 in a pattern reminiscent of that of thymic T cells. The immunophenotype also differs from that of NK cells (dark blue) and B cells (cyan). Note the presence of variable cCD79a, a relatively common finding in T-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma and not indicative of B lineage.

This biopsy shows a diffuse infiltrate of atypical lymphoid cells (<<36475>>). Giemsa illustrates medium-sized cells with scant cytoplasm and round to irregular nuclear contours (<<36477>>). Medium-sized atypical lymphoid cells display irregular nuclear contours, small nucleoli, and finely dispersed chromatin. Note the presence of several mitotic figures (<<36476>>).

The lymph node architecture is effaced by diffuse sheets of mononuclear cells that extend into perinodal soft tissue. More limited lymph node involvement by acute lymphoblastic leukaemia may show infiltration confined to the subcapsular sinus with inconspicuous spread into the underlying lymph node (<<36486>>). Touch imprint at triage of the fresh lymph node highlights the monotonous morphology and fine chromatin of the lymphoblasts (<<36490>>). The neoplastic cells are small to intermediate-sized lymphoid cells with finely stippled nuclear chromatin, scant cytoplasm, and conspicuous associated mitoses (<<36487>>). Immunohistochemistry shows that the neoplastic cells express TdT (nuclear localization) (<<36488>>). Immunohistochemistry shows neoplastic cells expressing CD3 (cytoplasmic localization, weak expression) among non-neoplastic T cells expressing both cytoplasmic and membranous CD3 (strong expression) (<<36489>>).

diagnosis: Histopathology of T-lymphoblastic leukaemia at diagnosis
legend: Bone marrow aspirate smear (Wright–Giemsa staining). The lymphoblasts may vary slightly in size, particularly on air-dried smears. The morphology of T-lymphoblastic leukaemia is indistinguishable from that of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia. Both may show eccentric orientation of scant cytoplasm (hand-mirror cells).
